newsitem.title: USA: Westinghouse Air buys Vapor from Mark IV.
newsitem.headline: Westinghouse Air buys Vapor from Mark IV.

text.p: Westinghouse Air Brake Co., North America's largest manufacturer of air brakes, said Thursday it acquired Vapour Corp. from Mark IV Industries Inc. for about $65 million.
Vapour is the leading U.S. manufacturer of door systems for transit rail cars and metropolitan buses, with about 575 employees in Chicago, Montreal and London.
The purchase price includes $63 million in cash and $2 million in potential payments tied to future sales targets.

Westinghouse Air Brake said a large portion of the projected increase in revenue is expected to come from new contracts for Vapour to provide door systems for the London Underground, a project that has already begun.

The deal is not expected to affect earnings per share for the remaining four months in the fiscal year, which ends Dec. 31, the company said. It is expected to contribute to earnings beginning in the first quarter of 1997.
Wilmerding, Pa.-based Westinghouse Air Brake makes air brakes and related equipment for locomotives, railway freight cars and passenger transit rail vehicles.
Westinghouse's stock fell 25 cents to $11.875 early on the New York Stock Exchange. Mark IV edged down 12.5 cents to $21.375, also on the NYSE.
